REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for Fragile X syndrome

METHODOLOGY
PCR-based assay for detection of CGG repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene promoter region. This assay accurately determines the number of CGG repeats and can detect normal, premutation, and full mutation alleles. The normal range is 6-45 CGG repeats, premutation range is 55-200 repeats, and full mutations contain >200 repeats.

RESULTS
FMR1 CGG Repeat Analysis:
Allele 1: 30 (±1) CGG repeats

Result: NORMAL

INTERPRETATION
This patient has a normal FMR1 allele with 30 (±1) CGG repeats, which is within the normal range (6-45 repeats). This result indicates that Fragile X syndrome due to FMR1 CGG repeat expansion is unlikely.

It should be noted that less than 1% of Fragile X syndrome cases may be caused by point mutations or other rearrangements within the FMR1 gene that are not detected by this PCR-based repeat expansion assay. If clinical suspicion remains high, additional testing such as FMR1 gene sequencing may be considered.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
